newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai gold market holds out for Indian festivals.
newsitem.headline: Dubai gold market holds out for Indian festivals.

text.p: Dubai's gold market is expected in the next few weeks to gradually recover from subdued summer business as demand picks up ahead of India's traditional wedding and festival season.
"Things are looking up. The monsoon has now come to an end and India's festivals and weddings are due to start in October," said one trader.
"We will start to see a gradual movement on the upside," he added.
Dubai is the main feeder market into India which is the world's single largest gold market. The Gulf Arab emirate provides some 80 percent of annual Indian demand of 477 tonnes.
Latest World Gold Council figures put Dubai gold imports at 29,890 kg in July, up from 26,334 kg in the same month last year. In June 1996 Dubai imported 28,392 kg.
Traders said the price of the local benchmark Ten Tola bar was down at an average 5,343 dirhams ($1,455) in the week compared to a previous 5,367 dirhams.
The drop in the price of the TT bar -- 3.746 ounces of 24 carat gold -- mirrored a slip in the world price for the yellow metal to $386.50/387.00 an ounce on Saturday from $388.20/70 a week earlier.

While most traders were optimistic about a rise in demand from India in the near term, one said Pakistan did not have much to offer. "Pakistan is slow. The money market is a little bit tight," he said.
